title: 📘 UNIT 4: SOCIETY AND POLITICS IN THE AGE OF WORLD WARS (1914–1945)
notes:
World War I → 1914–1918.
Russian Revolution → 1917.
Interwar Period → 1919–1939.
World War II → 1939–1945.

Major themes → alliance systems, nationalism, imperial rivalry, revolution, economic depression, Fascism, Nazism and global warfare.

title: 4.1 🌍 World War I and Its Settlement
notes:
World War I → global conflict from 1914 to 1918, also called the First World War, Great War and War to End All Wars.

Major causes:
• Militarism.
• Alliance systems.
• Imperialism.
• Nationalism.
• Rivalry among European powers.
• Balkan tensions.

Immediate cause → assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie by Gavrilo Princip on 28 June 1914.

Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July 1914.

title: 4.1.1 🤝 Alliance Systems of World War I
notes:
🔴 Triple Alliance / Central Powers:
• Germany.
• Austria-Hungary.
• Italy initially.

🔵 Triple Entente / Allied Powers:
• Britain.
• France.
• Russia.

Important developments:

• 1879 → Dual Alliance between Germany and Austria-Hungary.

• 1882 → Italy joined → Triple Alliance.

• 1891–1894 → Franco-Russian Alliance.

• 1904 → Entente Cordiale between Britain and France.

• 1907 → Britain and Russia settled differences → Triple Entente.

title: 4.1.2 ⚔️ Course of World War I
notes:
Western Front → Germany vs Allied Powers.
Eastern Front → Germany/Austria-Hungary vs Russia.

Schlieffen Plan → German plan to defeat France quickly by attacking through Belgium before concentrating against Russia.

Britain entered the war after Germany violated Belgian neutrality.

Major battles:
• Marne.
• Tannenberg.
• Ypres.
• Gallipoli.
• Verdun.
• Jutland.
• Somme.
• Amiens.

Trench warfare → defensive warfare using interconnected trenches.

New weapons → machine guns, artillery, chemical weapons, aircraft, tanks and submarines.

title: 4.1.3 🇺🇸🇷🇺 Turning Points and End of WWI
notes:
1917 → Russian Revolution led Russia to withdraw from the war.

3 March 1918 → Treaty of Brest-Litovsk ended Russia's participation.

6 April 1917 → USA entered the war against the Central Powers after Germany continued unrestricted submarine warfare.

1918 → Allied offensives weakened and disintegrated the Central Powers.

11 November 1918 → Germany signed the armistice; World War I ended.

title: 4.1.4 📉 Effects of World War I
notes:
• Millions of soldiers and civilians died or were wounded.
• Massive destruction of property and infrastructure.
• European economies weakened.
• Four major empires collapsed → German, Austro-Hungarian, Ottoman and Russian.
• Russian Revolution and rise of communism.
• New states and borders appeared in Europe.
• Nationalism increased.
• Germany's defeat and unresolved issues contributed to the rise of Nazism and World War II.
• New military technologies changed warfare.

title: 4.1.5 📜 Peace Settlement after WWI
notes:
Major treaties:

• Versailles → Germany, June 1919.

• Saint-Germain → Austria, September 1919.

• Neuilly → Bulgaria, November 1919.

• Trianon → Hungary, June 1920.

• Sèvres → Ottoman Turkey, August 1920.

Big Four:
• Woodrow Wilson → USA.
• Georges Clemenceau → France.
• David Lloyd George → Britain.
• Vittorio Orlando → Italy.

📌 The peace negotiations were held mainly in Paris during 1919–1920.

title: 4.1.6 🇩🇪 Treaty of Versailles
notes:
Signed → 28 June 1919.

Germany:
• Lost territories in Europe.
• Lost all colonies.
• Army limited to 100,000 men.
• Conscription prohibited.
• No military aircraft, tanks, heavy artillery or submarines.
• Rhineland demilitarized.
• Required to pay reparations.
• Accepted responsibility for war damages.

📌 The treaty was imposed on Germany and created strong resentment.

title: 4.1.7 🌙 Middle East Peace Settlement
notes:
The Ottoman Empire was divided after World War I.

Britain received mandates over:
• Iraq.
• Palestine.
• Transjordan.

France received mandates over:
• Syria.
• Lebanon.

📌 British and French influence increased in the Middle East after the collapse of Ottoman rule.

title: 4.2 🇷🇺 The Russian Revolution of 1917
notes:
Russian Revolution → political upheaval that ended Tsarist rule and eventually brought the Bolsheviks to power.

Main causes:
• Autocratic rule of Tsar Nicholas II.
• Poor social and economic conditions.
• Peasant land problems.
• Industrial workers' hardships.
• Political repression.
• Military defeats and suffering during World War I.
• Food shortages and inflation.

Two major phases:
• February Revolution.
• October Revolution.

title: 4.2.1 👑 February Revolution
notes:
February 1917 → strikes, demonstrations and food shortages led to the collapse of Tsar Nicholas II's government.

Nicholas II abdicated.

A Provisional Government was established.

📌 The monarchy ended, but Russia remained involved in World War I.

title: 4.2.2 ☭ Lenin and the April Theses
notes:
Vladimir Lenin → leader of the Bolsheviks.

April Theses → Lenin's program calling for:
• No support for the Provisional Government.
• Immediate peace.
• Land to peasants.
• Transfer of power to the Soviets.
• Preparation for socialist revolution.

Bolshevik slogan → "Peace! Bread! Land!" and "All Power to the Soviets!"

title: 4.2.3 ☭ October Revolution
notes:
25 October 1917 → Bolsheviks led by Lenin overthrew the Provisional Government.

New government → Soviet Council of People's Commissars.

Lenin → head of government.
Trotsky → major Bolshevik leader and organizer of the Red Army.

March 1918 → Treaty of Brest-Litovsk ended Russia's war with the Central Powers.

📌 The October Revolution marked the beginning of the spread of communism in the 20th century.

title: 4.3 📉 Interwar Period: Capitalist Economy, Fascism and Nazism
notes:
Interwar Period → period between World War I and World War II.

Major developments:
• Economic instability.
• Great Depression.
• Political extremism.
• Rise of dictatorships.
• Fascism in Italy.
• Nazism in Germany.
• Growth of militarism and expansionism.

title: 4.3.1 💥 Great Depression (1929–1933)
notes:
Great Depression → severe global economic crisis beginning in 1929 and lasting through the early 1930s.

Major features:
• Bank failures.
• Unemployment.
• Decline in industrial production.
• Falling prices and incomes.
• Collapse of international trade.
• Decline in agricultural and raw-material prices.

Political effects:
• Increased social unrest.
• Strengthened extremist movements.
• Helped militarists gain power in Japan.
• Helped Hitler and the Nazis gain power in Germany.

title: 4.3.2 🇺🇸 New Deal
notes:
New Deal → economic recovery program introduced by U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt from 1933.

Main aims:
• Stimulate economic recovery.
• Create employment.
• Regulate economic activity.
• Increase workers' wages.
• Redistribute wealth.
• Restore purchasing power.

📌 The New Deal used government intervention to address the effects of the Great Depression.

title: 4.3.3 🇮🇹 Fascism in Italy
notes:
Fascism → authoritarian and ultranationalist political ideology emphasizing strong leadership, nationalism, militarism and suppression of opposition.

Benito Mussolini → leader of Italian Fascism.

1922 → Mussolini came to power after the March on Rome.

Main features:
• Dictatorship.
• Extreme nationalism.
• Militarism.
• One-party rule.
• Suppression of opposition.
• Glorification of war.
• State control over political life.
• Expansionism.

title: 4.3.4 🇩🇪 Nazism in Germany
notes:
Nazism → German form of Fascism based on extreme nationalism, dictatorship, militarism, racism and expansionism.

Adolf Hitler → leader of the Nazi Party.

1933 → Hitler became Chancellor of Germany.

Mein Kampf → book written by Hitler while in prison.

Main features:
• One-party dictatorship.
• Extreme nationalism.
• Militarism.
• Anti-Semitism.
• Racist ideology.
• Suppression of political opposition.
• Territorial expansion.
• State propaganda.

title: 4.4 ⚔️ World War II
notes:
World War II → global conflict from 1939 to 1945.

Major causes:
• Unresolved issues of World War I.
• Harshness of the Versailles settlement.
• Rise of Fascism and Nazism.
• Economic crisis and Great Depression.
• German, Italian and Japanese expansionism.
• Failure of the League of Nations.
• Policy of appeasement.
• Militarization and rearmament.

title: 4.4.1 🤝 Alliance Systems of World War II
notes:
🔴 Axis Powers:
• Germany.
• Italy.
• Japan.

🔵 Allied Powers:
• Britain.
• France.
• Poland initially.
• Soviet Union.
• United States.
• China.

1936 → Rome-Berlin Axis.
27 September 1940 → Tripartite Pact formally united Germany, Italy and Japan.

title: 4.4.2 🕊️ Appeasement and Road to War
notes:
Appeasement → policy of making political or territorial concessions to Hitler in an attempt to avoid war.

Major developments:
• 1933 → Germany withdrew from the League of Nations.
• 1936 → Rhineland remilitarized.
• 1938 → Austria annexed (Anschluss).
• 1938 → Sudetenland annexed after Munich Agreement.
• 1938 → Germany occupied most of Czechoslovakia.
• April 1939 → Italy occupied Albania.

📌 Appeasement failed to stop German expansion.

title: 4.4.3 🇵🇱 Outbreak and Blitzkrieg
notes:
1 September 1939 → Germany invaded Poland.

3 September 1939 → Britain and France declared war on Germany.

Blitzkrieg → "lightning war"; rapid coordinated attacks using aircraft and fast-moving ground forces.

📌 Germany initially achieved rapid victories using Blitzkrieg tactics.

title: 4.4.4 🌍 Course of World War II
notes:
Major developments:
• Germany occupied much of Western Europe.
• Britain resisted German attacks.
• Germany invaded the Soviet Union in Operation Barbarossa, 1941.
• Japan expanded across East Asia and the Pacific.
• 7 December 1941 → Japan attacked Pearl Harbor.
• USA entered the war.
• Allied forces gradually turned the war against the Axis Powers.
• D-Day → Allied landing in Normandy, 6 June 1944.
• Germany surrendered in May 1945.

title: 4.4.5 🇯🇵 End of World War II
notes:
8 May 1945 → Germany surrendered; V-E Day.

Atomic bombs:
• 6 August 1945 → Hiroshima.
• 9 August 1945 → Nagasaki.

15 August 1945 → Emperor Hirohito announced Japan's unconditional surrender.

📌 World War II ended in 1945 after the defeat of the Axis Powers.

title: 4.4.6 💀 Consequences of World War II
notes:
• Massive loss of human life.
• Destruction of cities and infrastructure.
• European economic decline.
• Germany and Japan defeated and occupied.
• United States and Soviet Union emerged as major world powers.
• Colonial systems weakened.
• National liberation movements expanded.
• International cooperation increased.
• United Nations was established in 1945.
• Cold War rivalry developed between the USA and USSR.
